metadata.title: Two Fronts.
metadata.note: Month one (May 2026). Month-as-a-whole structure, not week-by-week. Third-person, Varun named; no other non-professor names. Runtime cap 3:30. Synthetic visuals only.

beats.narration_text: Month one on the Medhavy project ran two technical duties at the same time. Prompt engineering on the electron-microscopy textbook, and healthcare systems integration research against a live clinical API. Both started in the first week. Neither waited for the other.

send button arms terracotta; running indicator reads 'compiling month one…'
three result lines land — the month's three claims

props.command: Show me what Varun built on Medhavy in month one — the work, the findings, and the hours.
output: two technical duties, running in parallel

beats.narration_text: The first duty was the electron-microscopy textbook. Varun pushed prompt changes to a dedicated branch rather than straight to main, and repaired what was breaking in production: equation rendering, image handling, the cover page. That work later merged into the textbook repository as a pull request.

show.event: eyebrow sets: DUTY I — PROMPT ENGINEERING
title sets in the serif beneath the terracotta rule
thesis wipes in
three evidence bullets land as each is named

props.label: DUTY I — PROMPT ENGINEERING
props.thesis: Repairs that shipped to the repository.
bullets: HELIX prompt pushed to the improve-helix-prompt branch.
Equation rendering, image handling and cover page fixed.

beats.narration_text: Changing a prompt an entire textbook's tutor depends on is not a small edit, which is why it went to its own branch. The rendering repairs were the visible half: equations failing to typeset, image paths resolving wrong, a cover that would not build into the self-contained output.

show.event: artifact card titled improve-helix-prompt fades up
the repair lines set in mono, one per fix
spark line lands: 'Branch, not main.'

beats.narration_text: The second duty was healthcare systems integration research, run against Epic's FHIR sandbox. Not a tutorial environment — a real API with real authentication. Varun built the extraction end to end: test patient identifiers, the bulk group identifier, and nested demographic records flattened into something analysable.

show.event: eyebrow sets: DUTY II — HEALTHCARE INTEGRATION
title sets in the serif
thesis wipes in
bullets land as spoken

props.label: DUTY II — HEALTHCARE INTEGRATION
bullets: Test patient IDs and the Bulk FHIR Group ID extracted.
Nested FHIR demographics flattened to CSV.
Clinical documents retrieved, parsed and LLM-formatted.

beats.narration_text: Two scripts carry the pipeline. The first flattens nested demographic structures into a single file. The second pulls six clinical categories into six: problems, encounter diagnoses, labs, social history, encounters, diagnostic reports.

show.event: code card fades up; the two filenames set in mono
the six clinical categories list down the card as they are named
spark line lands: 'Six categories, six files.'

fetch_health_data.py → six CSVs

  encounter diagnoses   social history

format_responses.py → all_responses.md

beats.narration_text: One piece of friction is worth naming. The repository access needed to open that pull request took a week to become usable — the invite had been sent, and sat unread. Once open, the fixes went in as a proper pull request.

show.event: heavy ink rule draws; ground shifts to the friction register
label sets: 'Repository access'
'Requested May 7' and 'Open May 14' anchor the span; bar fills terracotta as days run to 7
resolution line wipes in — merged as a pull request

props.label: Repository access
props.resolution: Once granted, the fixes went in as a pull request — not an informal patch.

beats.narration_text: Retrieving the note text returned a four-oh-three Forbidden. The move that matters is not retry logic — it is reading what the server is refusing. A missing OAuth scope, system slash Binary dot read, resolved through the developer portal. Not a defect. A permission the token never had.

show.event: the 403 response line sits alone at the top of the card
diagnosis lines type beneath it
the missing scope highlights terracotta as it is spoken
spark line lands: 'Not a bug. A scope.'

props.title: GET /Binary/{id} → 403 Forbidden
props.code:
# not a code defect — an authorization gap

missing scope:  system/Binary.read
fix:            Epic developer portal → permission update
result:         note text retrieves clean

beats.narration_text: Then the finding that mattered more than the fix. Across the whole sandbox, seven patient records were populated, and sparsely. That is not enough to build research on. Varun reported it in writing to Prof. Sridhar, with a summarised spreadsheet of the sandbox API and an offer to explore further endpoints.

show.event: heavy ink rule draws across the top; ground shifts to the finding register
label sets: 'Sandbox data sparsity'
'Flagged May 15' anchors the span; the bar fills terracotta
'Reported to: Prof. Sridhar' sets beneath
resolution line wipes in — seven populated records, escalated with evidence

props.label: Sandbox data sparsity
props.resolution: Seven populated patient records. Reported upward with a spreadsheet, not worked around.

beats.narration_text: Prof. Sridhar ended the Epic integration workstream, citing accumulated blockers — sparse data, authorization friction, an unclear access model. Every one of them already documented from Varun's side. The same day brought a new assignment: Manim instructional video for the physics mechanics textbook, with access requested that day.

bullets: Prof. Sridhar ends the EPIC integration workstream as infeasible.
Cited blockers match those documented in the weekly reports.
Same day: reassigned to Manim video for the physics textbook.

beats.narration_text: Four weeks, twenty hours documented in each. Eighty hours for the month. Status: in compliance.

beats.narration_text: Month one, then. Two technical duties in parallel from the first week. Textbook repairs merged to the repository. A clinical-data pipeline built end to end against a live API, including a real authorization fix. And a data limitation found, evidenced, and escalated.
